model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the “effect” values for various language models across different linguistic categories. The horizontal axis, labeled with categories such as “IE-Baltic,” “IE-Germanic,” “IE-Indic,” “IE-Romance,” “IE-Slavic,” “IE-other,” “Isolate,” “Semitic,” and “Uralic,” displays these linguistic groupings. The vertical axis, representing “effect,” ranges from 0 to approximately 30 and uses a linear scale with tick intervals of 5, starting at 0 and incrementing upwards. Each bar corresponds to a specific language model, with the bars colored differently to distinguish between “mBERT-L2” (light blue), “XLM-L2” (green), “mBERT-R2” (purple), “mBERT-B2” (red), and “XLM-B2” (dark blue). The “mBERT-L2” bar reaches a height of approximately 23, with error bars extending approximately 3 units above and below the main bar.  The “XLM-L2” bar achieves a height of approximately 19, accompanied by similar error bars.  The “mBERT-R2” bar is represented at about 14, with error bars of roughly 2 units. The “mBERT-B2” bar is approximately 11, and has error bars of approximately 1.5 units, while the “XLM-B2” bar is around 8 with error bars of approximately 1 unit. All bars appear to be unsorted, and no bars are visually emphasized.
